theory.intro: The **relative velocity** of $A$ with respect to $B$ is how $A$ appears to move to someone travelling with $B$. It is found by subtracting the reference object's velocity: $\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}=\underset{\sim}{v}_{A}-\underset{\sim}{v}_{B}$.
facts: Reversing the order reverses the vector, because $\underset{\sim}{v}_{BA}=-\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}$.
The relative **speed** is the magnitude $|\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}|$, found by Pythagoras from its components.
A boat's velocity relative to the ground is its velocity in still water plus the velocity of the current.
To travel in a required direction, the still-water velocity needed is the required ground velocity minus the current.
A **bearing** is the angle measured clockwise from north, written with three figures from $000^{\circ}$ to $360^{\circ}$.

When both components are nonzero, use $\tan^{-1}$ on their magnitudes for the acute angle, then use a sketch of the vector to decide the bearing. If exactly one component is zero, read the direction directly as north, east, south or west. The zero vector has no direction and no bearing.
If both objects have constant velocities, then relative to $B$, object $A$ has constant velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}$, so their gap changes by $t\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}$ in time $t$.
steps: Write both velocities in component form
Subtract the reference object's velocity to get the relative velocity
Find the magnitude for the relative speed
Find the direction as a bearing, using a sketch to fix the quadrant

workedExamples.question_text: Car $A$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}34\\12\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and car $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}18\\24\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$ and its relative speed.

The velocity of vehicle $A$ relative to vehicle $B$ is $\begin{pmatrix}-8\\11\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Vehicle $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}32\\-4\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the velocity and speed of $A$.

Ship $A$ has velocity $4\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and ship $B$ has velocity $9\underset{\sim}{i}+15\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north. Find the bearing on which $A$ appears to move from $B$, to the nearest degree.
A ferry travels due north at $12$ km/h relative to the water. A current flows due east at $5$ km/h. Find the ferry's velocity relative to the bank, its speed and its bearing to the nearest degree.
A plane must have ground velocity $\begin{pmatrix}0\\280\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. The wind has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}30\\-40\end{pmatrix}$ km/h. Find the plane's required velocity relative to the air.

A boat has speed $13$ km/h in still water. A current flows due east at $5$ km/h. The boat must travel due north relative to the bank. Find its steering bearing to the nearest degree and its speed relative to the bank.

At noon, drone $A$ is at $(2,3)$ km and drone $B$ is at $(14,7)$ km. Their constant velocities are $\begin{pmatrix}20\\8\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and $\begin{pmatrix}12\\14\end{pmatrix}$ km/h respectively. Find the position of $B$ relative to $A$ after $30$ minutes and their separation then.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Let $t$ be hours after noon. Then $30$ minutes is $0.5$ hours.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_A(0.5)&=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}+0.5\begin{pmatrix}20\\8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}12\\7\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_B(0.5)&=\begin{pmatrix}14\\7\end{pmatrix}+0.5\begin{pmatrix}12\\14\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}20\\14\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}_{BA}(0.5)&=\underset{\sim}{r}_B(0.5)-\underset{\sim}{r}_A(0.5)\\&=\begin{pmatrix}20\\14\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}12\\7\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}8\\7\end{pmatrix}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Separation}&=\sqrt{8^2+7^2}\\&=\sqrt{113}\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A launch is $42$ km due east of a patrol boat. Both travel due east at constant speeds: the launch at $12$ km/h and the patrol boat at $26$ km/h. How long does the patrol boat take to catch the launch?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Take $\underset{\sim}{i}$ due east.

$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}_{PL}&=26\underset{\sim}{i}-12\underset{\sim}{i}\\&=14\underset{\sim}{i}\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$

Relative to the launch, the patrol boat closes the $42$ km gap at $14$ km/h.

$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{42}{14}\\&=3\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
Car $A$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}60\\20\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and car $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}25\\-15\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
Find the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$.

Plane $P$ has velocity $180\underset{\sim}{i}-40\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and plane $Q$ has velocity $110\underset{\sim}{i}+60\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
Find the velocity of $Q$ relative to $P$.

Ship $S$ has velocity $12\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and ship $T$ has velocity $3\underset{\sim}{i}-7\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
How fast is $S$ moving relative to $T$?

A boat's velocity in still water is $9\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and the current has velocity $-3\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
Find the boat's velocity relative to the river bank.
foundation.solution_text:
Velocity relative to the bank
$=(9\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j})+(-3\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j})$
$=6\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h

foundation.question_text:
The velocity of a jet ski relative to a ferry is $5\underset{\sim}{i}-5\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north.
Find the bearing on which the jet ski appears to move from the ferry.
foundation.solution_text:
The vector is $5$ east and $5$ south, so it points south-east.
$\tan\theta=\frac{5}{5}$
$\theta=45^{\circ}$ east of south
Bearing
$=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$
$=135^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text:
Cyclist $A$ has velocity $3\underset{\sim}{i}+10\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and cyclist $B$ has velocity $9\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north.
Find the bearing on which $A$ appears to move from $B$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}$
$=(3\underset{\sim}{i}+10\underset{\sim}{j})-(9\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j})$
$=-6\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$
The vector is $6$ west and $6$ north, so it points north-west.
$\tan\theta=\frac{6}{6}$
$\theta=45^{\circ}$ west of north
Bearing
$=360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$
$=315^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
Ship $A$ has velocity $18\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and ship $B$ has velocity $6\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north.
Find the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$, its speed, and its bearing to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}$
$=(18\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j})-(6\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j})$
$=12\underset{\sim}{i}-5\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h
$|\underset{\sim}{v}_{AB}|$
$=\sqrt{12^{2}+(-5)^{2}}$
$=13$ km/h
The vector is $12$ east and $5$ south, so it points south-east.
$\tan\theta=\frac{12}{5}$
$\theta=67.38^{\circ}$ east of south
Bearing
$=180^{\circ}-67.38^{\circ}$
$=113^{\circ}$ to the nearest degree

development.question_text:
Aircraft $X$ has velocity $210\underset{\sim}{i}-15\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h and aircraft $Y$ has velocity $130\underset{\sim}{i}+45\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
How fast is $X$ moving relative to $Y$?

A ferry heads due north in still water at $8$ km/h.
A current flows due east at $6$ km/h.
Find the ferry's velocity relative to the sea bed, giving its speed and its bearing to the nearest degree.

A plane must have a velocity relative to the ground of $\begin{pmatrix}0\\350\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
The wind has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}40\\-30\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
Find the velocity the plane must have relative to the air.

At noon car $A$ is at the point $(0,0)$ with velocity $\begin{pmatrix}60\\0\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and car $B$ is at the point $(10,20)$ with velocity $\begin{pmatrix}30\\40\end{pmatrix}$ km/h, with distances in kilometres.
Find the position of $B$ relative to $A$ half an hour later.

A cargo ship $P$ sails due east at $10$ km/h and a patrol boat $Q$ sails due east at $25$ km/h.
At noon $P$ is $45$ km due east of $Q$.
How long does $Q$ take to catch $P$?
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}_{QP}$
$=25\underset{\sim}{i}-10\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=15\underset{\sim}{i}$ km/h
Relative to $P$, the boat $Q$ closes the $45$ km gap at $15$ km/h.
$t$
$=\frac{45}{15}$
$=3$ hours

mastery.question_text:
Two helicopters leave the same helipad at the same time.
Helicopter $A$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}90\\120\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and helicopter $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}150\\40\end{pmatrix}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north.
Find the bearing on which $B$ appears to move from $A$, to the nearest degree, and how far apart the helicopters are after $45$ minutes.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}_{BA}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}150\\40\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}90\\120\end{pmatrix}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}60\\-80\end{pmatrix}$ km/h
The vector is $60$ east and $80$ south, so it points south-east.
$\tan\theta=\frac{60}{80}$
$\theta=36.87^{\circ}$ east of south
Bearing
$=180^{\circ}-36.87^{\circ}$
$=143^{\circ}$ to the nearest degree
$|\underset{\sim}{v}_{BA}|$
$=\sqrt{60^{2}+(-80)^{2}}$
$=100$ km/h
They start together, so after $45$ minutes the gap is
$=0.75\times 100$
$=75$ km

mastery.question_text:
A boat travels at $10$ km/h in still water.
A current flows due south at $6$ km/h.
The boat must travel due east relative to the bank.
Find the bearing the boat must steer, to the nearest degree, and its resulting speed relative to the bank.

The velocity of car $A$ relative to car $B$ is $\begin{pmatrix}-14\\8\end{pmatrix}$ km/h, and car $B$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}54\\-17\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
Find the velocity of car $A$ and how fast car $A$ is travelling.
